statement: Which of the following describes all solutions of the inequality $|2x - 7| < 9$?

choices.misconception: I solved only $2x - 7 < 9$ and forgot that $2x - 7$ can also be negative.
I wrote $-9 < 2x - 7 < 9$ but subtracted 7 from each part instead of adding it.
I split the inequality into an or statement, which is the form for a greater-than inequality, not a less-than one.

hints: Rewrite it as the compound inequality $-9 < 2x - 7 < 9$ and solve all three parts together.

solutions.reliable: $|2x - 7| < 9$ means $-9 < 2x - 7 < 9$. Adding $7$: $-2 < 2x < 16$. Dividing by $2$: $-1 < x < 8$. Check: $x = 0$ gives $|-7| = 7 < 9$, while $x = 8$ gives $|9| = 9$, which is not less than $9$.
solutions.elegant: Divide inside and out by 2: $|2x - 7| < 9$ is the same as $|x - 3.5| < 4.5$, so $x$ is within $4.5$ of $3.5$, which means $-1 < x < 8$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
